To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the dead-time correction of the DPP system is very efficient and accurate, and that the DPP system can be applied to a wide range of high-rate radiation measurements.
the DPP system, with the addition of the proposed dead-time correction algorithm (DTCA), is able to provide accurate ICR measurements at rates up to 10(6) cps.
the DPP system is able to provide accurate dead-time corrections even in the presence of pile-up events, with a maximum dead-time correction error (DTCE) of less than 0.5% for ICRs up to 1 MHz.

the DPP dead-time correction algorithm is very effective and robust.

the DPP system is able to provide an accurate and fast dead-time corrected measurement of ICR and energy even for the most demanding applications, such as the measurement of the ICR and of the gamma-ray spectrum of a 137Cs source with a high-resolution HPGe detector.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DPP system is able to correct for the dead-time effect at any ICR and for any pulse shape, even for those pulses that are too short to be detected by the fast analysis.
the DPP system can provide the true ICR and the true pulse height and peaking time distributions at high ICR, even in the presence of a large dead-time.
the DPP system is a powerful tool for the study of dead-time correction in radiation measurements.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DPP system can correct for high-rate dead time (HDRDT), i.e. the time during which the detector is not sensitive to incoming radiation, with an accuracy of 10-5 at ICRs up to 106 s-1.
, with the proposed method, the DPP system is able to correct dead-time effects up to 90% of the ICR, while maintaining a good resolution on the energy spectrum.
the DPP system is capable of correcting dead-time effects at high ICR, even when the dead-time correction algorithm is not based on the true ICR, but only on the measured one.
